description: Composite three-panel figure (single row, panels a–c), each panel a Crussard–Jaoul (C–J) strain-hardening analysis plot for Fe–18Mn–10Al–xC steels: ln(dσ/dε) on the y-axis versus ln(ε) on the x-axis, both axes dimensionless. In every panel y runs 7–11 and x runs −6 to −1, with integer major ticks and no units printed. Data are shown as small open grey markers fitted by red piecewise-linear segments whose breakpoints are annotated with true-strain values. (a) 0.5C steel: two-stage behaviour, breakpoint labelled ε=0.025; the first segment descends steeply from just below the 10 gridline (at lnε ≈ −5.2) to just below the 8 gridline, the second declines gently ending about midway between the 7 and 8 gridlines. (b) 0.8C steel: two stages, breakpoint ε=0.022; a steeper first segment starting between the 10 and 11 gridlines, followed by a nearly horizontal second stage lying just below the 8 gridline. (c) 1.2C steel: three stages, breakpoints ε=0.026 and ε=0.137; steep first segment, a flat plateau at roughly 7.5, then a rising third segment ending just below 8. The group demonstrates that the C–J hardening description changes from two-stage (0.5C, 0.8C) to three-stage (1.2C).

subfigures.description: C–J plot of ln(dσ/dε) vs ln(ε) for 0.5C steel with open grey data points and two red fitted linear segments meeting at an annotated breakpoint ε=0.025. First stage falls steeply from just below the 10 gridline to just below 8; second stage declines gently to about midway between 7 and 8. Axes: y 7–11, x −6 to −1.

C–J plot of ln(dσ/dε) vs ln(ε) for 0.8C steel, two red fitted segments with annotated breakpoint ε=0.022. First stage is steeper and starts higher than in (a) (between the 10 and 11 gridlines); the second stage is nearly horizontal just below the 8 gridline to lnε ≈ −1.1.

C–J plot of ln(dσ/dε) vs ln(ε) for 1.2C steel with three red fitted segments and two annotated breakpoints, ε=0.026 and ε=0.137. Steep descending first stage, a flat plateau near 7.5, and a positive-slope third stage rising to just below the 8 gridline.

observations.observation: All three panels plot the same quantities: ln(dσ/dε) on the y-axis against ln(ε) on the x-axis, y from 7 to 11 and x from −6 to −1, with no units printed on either axis.
Data in each panel are plotted as small open grey markers overlaid with red piecewise-linear fits, i.e. the fitted stage boundaries are drawn, not the raw curve.
Panel (a) (labelled 'a' top-left) shows two fitted stages with the transition annotated in the panel as ε=0.025.
Panel (b) shows two fitted stages with the transition annotated as ε=0.022.
Panel (c) shows three fitted stages with two transitions annotated as ε=0.026 and ε=0.137; the third stage has a positive slope, unlike the second stages of (a) and (b).
The first-stage segment is steeper and starts at a higher ln(dσ/dε) in (b) (between the 10 and 11 gridlines) than in (a) (just below the 10 gridline).
The caption identifies the panels as (a) 0.5C steel, (b) 0.8C steel and (c) 1.2C steel, and names the ordinate/abscissa as ln(ds/dε) and lnε respectively.
The citing text states that 0.5C and 0.8C steels exhibit a two-stage strain hardening, while 1.2C steel manifests a three-stage strain hardening.
The citing text states that the slope in the first stage is slightly steeper in 0.8C steel than in 0.5C steel.

The citing text states that in the second stage the strain hardening of 0.8C steel is somewhat stronger and extends to higher strains than that of 0.5C steel (Figs. 4 and 5); Fig. 5 shows the 0.8C second stage as near-horizontal whereas the 0.5C second stage still declines.
The citing text attributes the slightly faster decline of strain hardening in 0.8C than 0.5C to the presence of κ carbides in the austenitic phase, not to a change of hardening stage.
The citing text states that for the present 0.8C steel a modified C–J analysis showed no obvious descending behaviour in the second stage, unlike their previous Fe–12Mn–8Al–0.8C steel.

The citing text states that C–J analysis describes the sensitivity of strain hardening to internal lattice defects such as dislocation density and twin volume fraction, and links the three-stage behaviour of 1.2C steel to a different deformation mechanism.

measured_quantities: stage-transition true strain ε (dimensionless, annotated as 0.025, 0.022, 0.026 and 0.137)
unreadable_items: Individual data-point coordinates cannot be read exactly; only the annotated breakpoint strains are printed, so the ln(dσ/dε) values of the fit segments can only be located relative to gridlines.
Marker shapes (circle vs square) are too small to distinguish reliably at the supplied resolution.
Minor tick labels on both axes are not printed, so only integer major ticks can be reported.
